question: A point P is 13 cm away from the center of a circle. A tangent is drawn from P to the circle, and its length is 12 cm. What is the area of the circle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The radius, tangent, and distance to the center form a right-angled triangle.

Radius r = √(Distance² − Tangent²)

⇒ r = √(13² − 12²) = √(169 − 144) = √25 = 5 cm.

Area of circle = πr² = π × 5² = 25π cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 25π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of point P from the center of the circle O (OP) = 13 cm

Length of the tangent drawn from P (PT) = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

The tangent to a circle is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. Therefore, ΔOTP is a right-angled triangle at T.

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

Area of a circle = πr²

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔOTP, OP² = OT² + PT²

⇒ 13² = r² + 12²

⇒ 169 = r² + 144

⇒ r² = 169 − 144

⇒ r² = 25

⇒ r = √25 = 5 cm

⇒ Area of the circle = π × (5)²

⇒ Area = 25π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 25π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent Properties

A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point. The radius drawn from the center to the point of tangency is always strictly perpendicular to the tangent line.

Two Tangents from an External Point

If two tangents are drawn from a single external point to a circle, their lengths are always equal, and they subtend equal angles at the center.

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

Length of DCT = √[d² − (r₁ − r₂)²], where d is the straight-line distance between the centers and r₁, r₂ are the radii of the two circles.

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

Length of TCT = √[d² − (r₁ + r₂)²]. The TCT crosses the connecting line segment joining the centers of the two circles.
